No — Cormorant Mobile Detailing does NOT do ceramic coating.

Their own site says explicitly: "doesn't do ceramic coating, and its longest-lasting paint protection is the 6-month paint sealant."

What that means for your new Model Y in 94114:

Your Model Y is in their midsize / Class B group — the site lists Tesla Model Y as the example for Class B (sedans, crossovers and two-row SUVs).

Closest thing to multi-year protection they offer is:

1. The Flagship (polish-and-seal detail) — everything in the full detail + clay bar, one-step machine polish, 6-month paint sealant, plus upholstery/carpet shampoo.
- $629 for midsize, before fees/tax. In 94114 there is $0 travel fee.
- With 8.625% sales tax = ~$683.25 total, assuming no surcharges, generator / Saturday fees.
- Takes 6-8 hours, must start in morning window, and owner Ines does every Flagship herself on Wed/Thu/Fri mornings only.
- $150 deposit to book, counts toward total.

2. Cheaper shorter option — Full detail (The Schooner) + clay + sealant add-ons:
- $249 (full, midsize) + $70 clay + $115 sealant = $434 before tax, ~$471.43 with tax. Sealant can only be bought together with clay on an exterior wash or full detail.

Important limits:
- They don't clay / polish / seal matte, satin paint or vinyl wraps — if your Y has one of those, Flagship and sealant aren't available.
- They don't do multi-stage paint correction / swirl removal — only the one-step polish in The Flagship.
- They serve 94114 with no travel fee.

The Bay Auto Pages directory listing that says "ceramic coating" is out of date (last updated March 2023) — Cormorant's own site is current as of Sept 2026 and says not offered, so go with the site.

If you want true multi-year ceramic, you'll need a different shop — Cormorant can only do the 6-month sealant.

Straight answer: No — paying for Cormorant's top package will not guarantee that key scratch comes out.

Your description — deep enough that your fingernail catches — is the classic sign it has likely gone through the clear coat, and Cormorant says on its own site:

> Whether The Flagship's one-step polish will remove a particular scratch isn't known until a technician inspects it, because the answer depends on whether the scratch has gone through the clear coat.

Other important fine print from Cormorant:

- Its only machine polish is the one-step polish in The Flagship — it does NOT do multi-stage paint correction. For buffing / polish / swirl removal, the Flagship is all they offer.
- Its free re-do promise does NOT cover stains or scratches that were already there.

So you could pay $549+ and still have the scratch visible. If removal is your only goal, get an in-person inspection first — or get a quote from a body shop / paint-correction specialist — before booking the Flagship for scratch removal.

For reference, for your Mazda3 in 94131:
- Top package = The Flagship (everything in full detail + clay bar + one-step machine polish + 6-month sealant + shampoo)
- Mazda3 = small / Class A = $549 before tax/fees, no travel fee in 94131. With 8.625% sales tax = ~$596.35 before any surcharges or Saturday/generator fees. $150 deposit to book.
